assessment_policy.construct_validity: Define the interpretation and use of evidence first; align task, scoring and intended inference to the learning outcome.
assessment_policy.reliability: Consistency must be evaluated from actual repeated or multi-rater observations; rubric structure alone does not establish reliability.
assessment_policy.fairness: Remove irrelevant barriers while preserving the target construct; examine language, disability, device, cost, regional and cultural assumptions.
assessment_policy.no_universal_score: Use criterion-level profiles; do not average unlike constructs into a universal learner score.
assessment_policy.evidence_provenance: Store task version, conditions, support, assessor role, accommodation, artifact reference and feedback/retry lineage.

assessment_instruments.construct_statement: The assessment samples whether the learner can: Break a real problem into inputs, outputs, constraints and smaller testable tasks.

primary_instrument.prompt: Given a new task, produce a decomposition with inputs, outputs, constraints and at least three edge cases. Produce this evidence: working code or pseudocode, test cases, execution trace, and short design rationale. State assumptions and support used. Explain how Decomposition, invariants, input/output contracts informed your decisions.
primary_instrument.expected_evidence: working code or pseudocode, test cases, execution trace, and short design rationale
primary_instrument.conditions: State tools, time, prompts, collaboration and accommodations. Use a parallel form for repeat assessment; preserve task version.

assessment_instruments.alternate_form: Equivalent form: complete the same outcome using a different example, representation or tool. Keep the same construct and success criteria; do not make the task easier or harder by changing irrelevant reading, device or time demands.
assessment_instruments.transfer_probe: Apply the same target to: Design a small feature from a user story.. Explain which principles remain and what must change.
assessment_instruments.delayed_retention_probe: After a delay chosen for this outcome, complete a cold check: Given a new task, produce a decomposition with inputs, outputs, constraints and at least three edge cases. Use a changed example and do not show the original worked solution.

scoring_rubric.criterion: Produces valid evidence that meets the stated outcome: Break a real problem into inputs, outputs, constraints and smaller testable tasks.

anchors.0_not_evident: No usable evidence, or the attempt is materially incorrect / unsafe.
anchors.1_emerging: Partial performance; important omissions or prompts are needed.
anchors.2_meets: Independently meets the stated outcome under the task conditions.
anchors.3_strong: Meets the outcome accurately and efficiently while handling a meaningful boundary case.

scoring_rubric.criterion: Uses and explains the relevant model: Decomposition, invariants, input/output contracts

anchors.0_not_evident: Cannot explain the model or explanation contradicts the evidence.
anchors.1_emerging: Names concepts but connections or reasoning are incomplete.
anchors.2_meets: Accurately explains the decisions and connects the model to the result.
anchors.3_strong: Explains causal/structural relationships, trade-offs and when the model is limited.

scoring_rubric.criterion: Checks the result against the task constraints and relevant safety/quality boundary: disposable local project; no credentials or destructive operations

anchors.0_not_evident: No meaningful check; ignores a critical constraint or boundary.
anchors.1_emerging: Performs a partial check but misses a relevant error, limitation or risk.
anchors.2_meets: Checks relevant constraints and identifies/corrects a plausible issue.
anchors.3_strong: Selects a proportionate verification method, explains residual uncertainty and respects all boundaries.

scoring_rubric.criterion: Adapts the outcome to a changed context: Design a small feature from a user story.

anchors.0_not_evident: Cannot apply the method to a changed case.
anchors.1_emerging: Transfers only with substantial prompting or copies the original pattern without adaptation.
anchors.2_meets: Adapts correctly to the changed case and explains what changed.
anchors.3_strong: Adapts robustly, anticipates a new edge case and explains limits of transfer.

interpretation_rules.reporting: Report criterion-level results, support level and conditions. Do not collapse all criteria into a universal percentage or rank.
interpretation_rules.independent_demonstration: Criterion A1 and any task-critical criterion must reach level 2 or above without step-by-step help; explain support conditions.
interpretation_rules.transfer: Report separately; a strong initial task does not imply transfer.
interpretation_rules.retention: Report separately after delayed probe; immediate performance cannot establish retention.
interpretation_rules.safety_gate: disposable local project; no credentials or destructive operations

feedback_sequence: Name one thing the learner did correctly, with evidence.
Identify the first consequential gap against a criterion.
Explain the relevant concept or procedure without giving away the full answer.
Offer one targeted practice action.
Reassess using the alternate form or a changed example.
feedback_and_retry.retry_policy: Keep original attempt and retry as separate append-only evidence. A retry may show learning after feedback but must not overwrite the initial independent result.
feedback_and_retry.stop_rule: Stop and redirect when task conditions breach the stated safety, privacy, consent, authorisation or supervision boundary.

accessibility_and_fairness.construct_preserving_accommodations: Offer alternative response modes (oral, written, diagram, assistive technology, low-bandwidth/offline) when the mode is not itself the target construct.
accessibility_and_fairness.do_not_accommodate_away: Do not remove a skill component that is explicitly part of the outcome (e.g. oral interaction when speaking is the target); instead adjust access barriers unrelated to the construct.
bias_checks: Reading load does not exceed what the objective requires.
Language accent, handwriting, device brand or internet speed are not scored unless directly relevant to the outcome.
Examples do not assume expensive tools, paid subscriptions or a specific country context unless required.
Scoring anchors describe observable evidence rather than personality or presumed effort.

State assumptions and support used. Explain how Feedback, reinforcement, shaping, variability, transfer informed your decisions.
primary_instrument.expected_evidence: scenario analysis, prediction, evidence distinction and alternative explanation
primary_instrument.conditions: State tools, time, prompts, collaboration and accommodations. Use a parallel form for repeat assessment; preserve task version.

assessment_instruments.alternate_form: Equivalent form: complete the same outcome using a different example, representation or tool. Keep the same construct and success criteria; do not make the task easier or harder by changing irrelevant reading, device or time demands.
assessment_instruments.transfer_probe: Apply the same target to: Build training protocols.. Explain which principles remain and what must change.

scoring_rubric.criterion: Produces valid evidence that meets the stated outcome: Explain practice, feedback and reinforcement without reducing learning to rewards.

anchors.0_not_evident: No usable evidence, or the attempt is materially incorrect / unsafe.
anchors.1_emerging: Partial performance; important omissions or prompts are needed.
anchors.2_meets: Independently meets the stated outcome under the task conditions.
anchors.3_strong: Meets the outcome accurately and efficiently while handling a meaningful boundary case.

scoring_rubric.criterion: Uses and explains the relevant model: Feedback, reinforcement, shaping, variability, transfer

anchors.0_not_evident: Cannot explain the model or explanation contradicts the evidence.
anchors.1_emerging: Names concepts but connections or reasoning are incomplete.
anchors.2_meets: Accurately explains the decisions and connects the model to the result.
anchors.3_strong: Explains causal/structural relationships, trade-offs and when the model is limited.

scoring_rubric.criterion: Checks the result against the task constraints and relevant safety/quality boundary: no diagnosis, coercive profiling or forced disclosure of personal experiences

anchors.0_not_evident: No meaningful check; ignores a critical constraint or boundary.
anchors.1_emerging: Performs a partial check but misses a relevant error, limitation or risk.
anchors.2_meets: Checks relevant constraints and identifies/corrects a plausible issue.
anchors.3_strong: Selects a proportionate verification method, explains residual uncertainty and respects all boundaries.

scoring_rubric.criterion: Adapts the outcome to a changed context: Build training protocols.

anchors.0_not_evident: Cannot apply the method to a changed case.
anchors.1_emerging: Transfers only with substantial prompting or copies the original pattern without adaptation.
anchors.2_meets: Adapts correctly to the changed case and explains what changed.
anchors.3_strong: Adapts robustly, anticipates a new edge case and explains limits of transfer.

interpretation_rules.transfer: Report separately; a strong initial task does not imply transfer.
interpretation_rules.retention: Report separately after delayed probe; immediate performance cannot establish retention.
interpretation_rules.safety_gate: no diagnosis, coercive profiling or forced disclosure of personal experiences

interpretation_rules.retention: Report separately after delayed probe; immediate performance cannot establish retention.

feedback_sequence: Name one thing the learner did correctly, with evidence.
Identify the first consequential gap against a criterion.
Explain the relevant concept or procedure without giving away the full answer.
Offer one targeted practice action.

feedback_and_retry.retry_policy: Keep original attempt and retry as separate append-only evidence. A retry may show learning after feedback but must not overwrite the initial independent result.
feedback_and_retry.stop_rule: Stop and redirect when task conditions breach the stated safety, privacy, consent, authorisation or supervision boundary.

accessibility_and_fairness.construct_preserving_accommodations: Offer alternative response modes (oral, written, diagram, assistive technology, low-bandwidth/offline) when the mode is not itself the target construct.
accessibility_and_fairness.do_not_accommodate_away: Do not remove a skill component that is explicitly part of the outcome (e.g. oral interaction when speaking is the target); instead adjust access barriers unrelated to the construct.
bias_checks: Reading load does not exceed what the objective requires.
Language accent, handwriting, device brand or internet speed are not scored unless directly relevant to the outcome.
Examples do not assume expensive tools, paid subscriptions or a specific country context unless required.
Scoring anchors describe observable evidence rather than personality or presumed effort.

calibration_protocol.purpose: Train raters to apply module-specific criteria consistently; distinguish construct evidence from presentation, confidence, effort and irrelevant access barriers.

sequence.name: Orientation
sequence.action: Read the target outcome, construct statement, conditions, rubric and safety boundary. Identify what is in-scope and explicitly out-of-scope.

sequence.name: Independent scoring
sequence.action: Both raters score the same response independently before discussion. Record criterion level, exact evidence quote/feature and uncertainty.

sequence.name: Compare
sequence.action: Compare criterion-level ratings. Record exact disagreement and whether it concerns construct interpretation, evidence sufficiency, anchor wording or missing context.

sequence.name: Adjudicate
sequence.action: Use rubric wording and observable evidence; document rationale. Do not average scores to hide disagreement.

sequence.name: Revise
sequence.action: If disagreement reveals ambiguity, revise the criterion or anchor and version the rubric; rescore affected samples.

sequence.name: Monitor
sequence.action: Recheck drift on a later common sample set; do not assume one calibration session permanently establishes reliability.

minimum_pilot_design.sample_design: At least 30 common evidence samples distributed across multiple disciplines and task types for an initial cross-domain check; plus discipline-specific samples for high-stakes or technically specialised outcomes.
minimum_pilot_design.scoring: Two raters independently score every common sample at criterion level. Keep raw scores and rationales.
minimum_pilot_design.metrics: Report exact agreement, adjacent agreement, criterion-level confusion matrices and weighted kappa or an appropriate ordinal agreement statistic where assumptions/sample size permit. For nominal/categorical ratings use a suitable coefficient. Report confidence intervals and prevalence effects; do not treat a single coefficient as validity.
minimum_pilot_design.threshold_policy: Do not set a universal pass threshold before the use case, stakes and consequences are defined. Any local operational threshold must be justified and reviewed.
minimum_pilot_design.limitations: A small or convenience sample yields unstable estimates. Cross-discipline aggregation can hide a weak rubric in one discipline; report by discipline and criterion where sample permits.

validity_review_matrix.question: Does the task sample the full intended outcome and exclude irrelevant material?
validity_review_matrix.evidence_needed: Outcome-task map; expert review; item/task coverage analysis.

validity_review_matrix.question: Do learners interpret instructions and use intended reasoning rather than guessing what the examiner wants?
validity_review_matrix.evidence_needed: Cognitive interviews or think-aloud pilot with consent; observed process notes.

validity_review_matrix.question: Do rubric dimensions behave as intended and remain distinguishable?
validity_review_matrix.evidence_needed: Criterion-level scoring data and analysis appropriate to sample size; no assumptions from rubric design alone.

validity_review_matrix.question: Do results relate plausibly to independent demonstrations and relevant external criteria?
validity_review_matrix.evidence_needed: Predefined comparison evidence; avoid circularly validating one ATHENA score with another ATHENA score.

validity_review_matrix.question: Are decisions fair, useful and free from avoidable construct-irrelevant barriers or harmful consequences?
validity_review_matrix.evidence_needed: Accessibility/bias review, learner feedback, subgroup analysis where ethically and statistically appropriate.

pilot_instruments.learner_cognitive_interview: Ask learner to paraphrase the task, describe what they think is being assessed, explain how they approached it, identify confusing language/device barriers, and reflect on feedback usefulness. Participation voluntary; age-appropriate consent/assent and privacy safeguards.
pilot_instruments.task_observation: Record time only if time is part of construct; note prompts, interruptions, tool availability, access needs and deviations from conditions.
pilot_instruments.delayed_retention: Schedule a later parallel-form task after an interval selected for the learning objective; record intervening practice rather than treating delay as a clean no-practice condition.
pilot_instruments.transfer: Use a new context with the same underlying construct and document how much context differs from the original.
